target_customer: Security teams at mid-size companies that want realistic social engineering and breach simulation (customers shown on its site include Eight Sleep, Everest Global Insurance, Fella Health and Precision Medicine Group)
problem: Phishing training and compliance checklists do not show whether help-desk vishing, deepfaked executives or MFA fatigue attacks would actually succeed against a company's people and controls.
business_model: B2B security SaaS and managed testing; a first campaign is offered at no cost
product_category: AI social engineering and breach and attack simulation

founders.name: Mohammad Eshan
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page. A search snippet from a directory mentions a CTO co-founder who was a senior AI engineer at BlackRock, but the YC page lists only one founder, so no co-founder is recorded.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs voice agents, deepfake generation and orchestration of multi-step attack chains with remediation checks. Standard AI engineering with some hard parts, and the founder's offensive security background supplies the attack playbooks.

defensibility.rationale: Several vendors already sold AI vishing and deepfake simulation in 2025 and the techniques are widely reproducible. Any edge comes from attack quality and the retest loop, not structural barriers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not determined. Search results show many vendors offering vishing and deepfake simulation, but no source dated at founding shows what they did about this specific wedge.

market_need_then: Search results from vendor and trade pages describe rising AI-driven vishing and deepfake attacks and many security awareness vendors adding simulation, which indicates demand. No dated spend figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses ghosteye.ai. No purchase history found.

identity.logo: Directory listings show a logo but no source describes it
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain security language: always-on red team, evidence that risk went down

brand_strength.rationale: Only directory listings and the YC page mention the brand. G2 lists an unrelated GhostEye video surveillance product, which makes the name confusable. No press about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: GhostEye is an active Summer 2025 company with a single listed founder who led red teams at BlackRock and worked on offensive operations at MITRE, which fits the product. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news was found. Funding is not verified beyond an aggregator figure, so the outcome so far is unknown and the company is early.
notes: Funding: one aggregator (StartupIntros) shows a $500K round dated 2025-06-01 and others label it pre-seed; unverified, so not recorded as a round and probably YC's standard deal. Competitors: only undated vendor pages (Breacher.ai, Brightside, Jericho, Adaptive Security, Threatcop, Hoxhunt, Keepnet) were found, so the dated list is empty. No outcome news found. Update: the $500K round dated 2025-06-01 is now recorded as a round (StartupIntros calls it seed; VCBacked and Zerogtalent call it pre-seed). It rests on aggregators and may be the standard YC deal. A Zerogtalent listing names a CTO co-founder (Charles Antoine Malenfant), but the YC page lists one founder, so he is not added.
